note.explanation: Structured data is organised and formatted to be easily searchable and analysable. Unstructured data is more free-form and doesn't fit into a specific format. Structured data is often stored in rows and columns, while unstructured data includes items such as emails, social media posts, videos, and images.
examples: A student spreadsheet with columns for Student ID, Name, Class, and Fee Status is structured data.
An email or a video is unstructured data.
note.checkAnswer: A student spreadsheet is structured data because it is organised in rows and columns. A video is unstructured data because it does not fit into that format.
note.simple: Structured data is neatly arranged. Unstructured data is not arranged in a fixed format.
note.checkQuestion: Is a spreadsheet of student records structured or unstructured data, and why?
note.title: Structured and Unstructured Data
steps: Look for a fixed arrangement, such as rows and columns.
If the data is arranged in a searchable format, identify it as structured data.
If it is free-form and does not fit a specific format, identify it as unstructured data.
note.answer: Structured data is organised in a format that is easy to search and analyse; unstructured data is free-form and does not fit a specific format.

explain.title: Data has two types
explain.body: With respect to storage and processing, data has two types: structured and unstructured data.

explain.title: Structured data
explain.body: Structured data is organised and formatted to be easily searchable and analysable. Examples include data in spread sheets and traditional databases. In a spreadsheet, each row is a record, such as a student, and each column is an attribute, such as Student ID or Fee Status.

explain.title: Unstructured data
explain.body: Unstructured data is more free-form and doesn't fit into a specific format. Examples include text from emails, social media posts, videos, and images. This type of data is harder to organise but can be very valuable.

explain.title: How to tell them apart
explain.body: Look at how the information is stored. A fixed, organised arrangement such as rows and columns is structured data. Free-form material that does not fit a specific format is unstructured data.

mistakes: Do not confuse a record with an attribute: in the spreadsheet example, a row is a record and a column is an attribute.
Do not say that structured data must be numbers; it can include names, dates, and fee statuses in an organised table.
Do not call emails, social media posts, videos, or images structured just because they are stored on a computer.
When defining unstructured data, include that it is free-form and does not fit a specific format.
